feedback: Judged before racing, so I state no outcome for this candidate. The evidence is the iteration-2 race (score 75.6, best so far): 60 trials, 0 finishes, every run off_track, progress 0.12 to 0.28 (best on oval), max_error about 0.065 m just past the 0.06 m limit, steering_oscillation rising to 0.15 to 0.24 when kp went to 5, and 1.0 to 1.75 line-loss events per run. That supports the diagnosis of a steady drift that kp alone cannot fix. The candidate changes the controller in a way that targets this: ki goes from 0.02 to 0.3 so the integral can cancel a constant motor-mismatch bias, kp drops from 5 to 4 to reduce overshoot, and kd rises to 0.5 to damp the jitter. The integral clamp of plus or minus 2 limits windup. All values are inside the contract limits. Sensor weights, footprint and line_loss policy are unchanged, so any change in result can be attributed to the controller. The main risk is speed. base_speed drops from 1.4 to 1.3, and the 3.0 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s average, so a finish may be out of reach even if the line is held. Approval is justified because this is early exploration with 8 iterations left, the change is a clear, testable response to the bias evidence, and a race is the only way to measure the integral effect. Interpreting the next race: if max_error falls below about 0.05 m and line_loss_events drops with progress near 1 but completion_time above 3.0 s, the line is being held and the speed is the limit, so raise base_speed to about 1.5 while keeping ki 0.3. If max_error still reaches 0.06 m with ki 0.3, the integral is too slow or too small, so raise ki to about 0.6 before touching kp. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 with ki high, the integral is causing overshoot, so lower ki to about 0.15 and keep kd at 0.5.
requested_changes: If the next race keeps the robot on the line (max_error below about 0.05 m) but completion_time is above 3.0 s or progress stalls short of 1, raise controller.base_speed to about 1.5 and keep ki at 0.3, since 1.3 is probably too slow for the 500-point completion bonus.

If max_error still reaches about 0.06 m with ki at 0.3, raise controller.ki to about 0.6 (the only change to the controller gains) before touching kp, since the iteration-2 drift was a steady bias that ki is meant to cancel.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 after the ki increase, lower controller.ki to about 0.15 and keep kd at 0.5, since the iteration-2 data showed that extra steering gain added overshoot.
